game_concept: A puzzle set in Coastal Port – Rope Walk, the rope-makers' walk: the sailor must handle jellyfish swarms while practicing conditionals (if / elif / else). Core idea – Discount Rules: Apply shop rules like if total >= 100 to give each customer the right discount.
theme: Coastal Port – Rope Walk: the rope-makers' walk
core_gameplay_loop: Construct a solution, execute it, inspect actual state and outputs, then revise until all mission goals pass.
player_objective: Debug ordering: Repair the reversed arithmetic instructions in the starter. add 16, then double. Match all 3 streams; preserve their order. Dataset 5, operand 16.
controls: Edit both node programs. IN reads the upstream queue; OUT sends to the next node. Step advances one cycle; Run checks every stream.
win_condition: The executed solution satisfies every output and world-state check.
lose_condition: The available unsuccessful execution checks are exhausted.
assets_style: Shared Kenney CC0 tile and audio assets with deterministic Canvas layouts; assets are not duplicated per game.
duplicate_check_notes: Unique combination of primary mechanic 'Discount Rules' (Week 3 slot 10), mission type 'Efficiency Trial', and setting 'Rope Walk'. No other file shares this combination; games sharing the mechanic differ in mission/win condition and setting, and games sharing the setting use a different mechanic.

region.name: Coastal Port
region.mood: sea-shanty accordion with wave and gull ambience

tutorial: Read the objective, fixtures and command reference.
Build the circuit or route, or edit the node/adventure program.
Use Step to inspect state; Run checks the real outputs and goals.
Revise errors before using the remaining execution checks.
source_player_objective: Reach the harbor bell using at most 14 actions, so every code step counts.
source_win_condition: The harbor bell reached with actions_used <= 14.
source_lose_condition: actions_used exceeds 14 before the harbor bell is reached, or lives reach 0.
hint: Follow the input through each operation. Compare every output, including negative inputs.
